chapter: New Orleans Rhythm Kings and Tin Roof Blues
title: His Tin Roof Blues trombone chorus
summary: He played what felt natural; everyone copies it, including Wingy's Tijuana trombonist.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Yeah. Is there anything of interest to your trombone soul, how you first, you might say, created that thing, you know, starting on that low note and all?
No, we just played . Then we played . Then rap took that high chorus, and it was printed to me and I played . Just played what felt natural.
Came into your head. Because everybody copies that, mostly note for note.
Windy won high trombone play, he says, can you play Brunus' chorus on tin roof? He says, if you can you get the job. He's got a kid from Mexico, he calls him the Brunus of Tijuana, Jack somebody.
Oh, he was up here once. Jack Flores? Yeah, sure, he was here at the 11-11 one time on a Sunday, I remember. And Wingy came through.
He calls him the Brunus of Tijuana.
Yeah, that's probably the most copied and most famous trombone song.
